llm.reply:
The gene product of KRAS is a GTPase enzyme [4]. The protein functions biologically as an intracellular molecular switch that stimulates downstream signaling pathways [26: "acts as a molecular switch to persistently stimulate downstream signaling pathways"].

## Small GTPase Superfamily

The protein produced by this gene belongs to the small GTPase superfamily [11: "encodes a protein that is a member of the small GTPase superfamily"]. It is a member of the mammalian ras gene family derived as a Kirsten ras oncogene homolog [11: "This gene, a Kirsten ras oncogene homolog from the mammalian ras gene family"].

## Oncogenic Activation

Activating mutations in the gene involve a single amino acid substitution [11: "A single amino acid substitution is responsible for an activating mutation"]. These alterations produce persistent activation of the protein to induce continuous downstream signaling [26: "mutations result in constitutive activation of the KRAS protein, which acts as a molecular switch to persistently stimulate downstream signaling pathways"].

The KRAS gene product functions as a GTPase enzyme [4][11: "encodes a protein that is a member of the small GTPase superfamily"]. Activated oncogenic protein constitutively signals downstream proliferation cascades [26: "acts as a molecular switch to persistently stimulate downstream signaling pathways, including cell proliferation and survival, thereby leading to tumorigenesis"]. The official gene symbol is KRAS [1].

## Gene Properties

The official gene name is KRAS [5]. The literature entity name is Kras [6]. An activating mutation in the sequence occurs via a single amino acid substitution [11: "A single amino acid substitution is responsible for an activating mutation"]. 

## Genomic Variants

The clinvar title is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.458ATG[1] (p.Asp154del) [3]. Another variant clinvar title is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.36T>C (p.Gly12=) [10]. A third clinvar title is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.337C>T (p.Leu113=) [15]. A fourth clinvar title is NM_033360.4(KRAS):c.524A>G (p.Glu175Gly) [19]. An additional clinvar title is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.417T>A (p.Ile139=) [23].

## Oncogenic Signaling

A pubmed title is Role of oncogenic KRAS in the prognosis, diagnosis and treatment of colorectal cancer [2]. Colorectal cancer progression involves KRAS-driven fibroblast remodeling to promote vascularization [28: "transforms the phenotype of carcinoma-associated fibroblasts (CAF) into lipid-laden CAFs, promoting angiogenesis and tumor progression"]. A pubmed title is Oncogenic KRAS Drives Lipofibrogenesis to Promote Angiogenesis and Colon Cancer Progression [14]. A publication pmid is 34742312 [8]. Another publication pmid is 37768068 [17]. A publication pmid is 34776511 [13].

## Targeted Therapeutics

Small molecules directly inhibit G12C alleles [27: "AMG510 was the first drug-targeting KRAS (G12C) to be approved for clinical use this year"]. A pubmed title is KRAS mutation: from undruggable to druggable in cancer [9]. Heterobifunctional degraders target multiple oncogenic variants [30: "designed a heterobifunctional small molecule that potently degrades 13 out of 17 of the most prevalent oncogenic KRAS alleles"]. A pubmed title is Targeting cancer with small-molecule pan-KRAS degraders [22]. A publication pmid is 39298590 [25]. In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, common mutations include G12D, G12V, and G12R [29: "the most common KRAS mutations in PDAC are G12D (44%), G12V (34%) and G12R (20%)"]. A pubmed title is Targeting KRAS in pancreatic cancer [18]. A publication pmid is 38686056 [21]. Clinical trial name entries include Sorafenib in Combination With Irinotecan in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Patients With KRAS Mutated Tumors [7], PREMIUM, Observational Study [12], A Trial of mFOLFIRI With MEK162 in Patients With Advanced RAS (HRAS, NRAS, or KRAS) Positive Metastatic Colorectal Cancers [16], Frequency of EGFR and KRAS Mutations and Clinical-prognostic Correlation in Brazilian Lung Cancer Patients [20], and A Phase 1/2, Study Evaluating the Safety, Tolerability, PK, and Efficacy of Sotorasib (AMG 510) in Subjects With Solid Tumors With a Specific KRAS Mutation (CodeBreaK 100) [24].
